entry.title: Shinji Mikami to Receive AIAS Hall of Fame Award at 2026 DICE Awards
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Shinji Mikami, a pioneer of the Resident Evil series, will be inducted into the Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences (AIAS) Hall of Fame at the 30th annual DICE Awards on February 18. Goichi Suda, CEO of Grasshopper Manufacture, is scheduled to present the award, recognizing Mikami's 30-year career in the gaming industry.

Mikami currently serves as the CEO of Unbound, a studio recently acquired by Stellar Blade developer Shift Up. He previously founded Tango Gameworks, the developer behind The Evil Within and Hi-Fi Rush.

entry.title: Andy 'TheFlow0' Nguyen Abandons PS5 Linux Project
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | frvr.com | source | hacker news

Developer and hacker Andy 'TheFlow0' Nguyen has announced his departure from the PlayStation 5 modding scene and the end of his work on the PS5 Linux project. Nguyen cited the rise of "vibe-coders"—individuals using large language models to submit code they do not understand—as a primary reason for leaving the open-source community.

The developer had previously planned to expand support to the PS5 Pro by 2027. The decision follows an incident in which AI-assisted users identified and reported a critical hypervisor bug to Sony for a bounty, a move that Nguyen argues compromises the future of console modification and the security of the modding community.

entry.title: Ink & Switch Introduces Playbook Programmable Notebook
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | youtube.com | discussion

Ink & Switch has unveiled Playbook, a project within its programmable ink track designed to create a digital notebook that combines the feel of paper with software dynamism. The system uses "material physics" and gestural inputs, allowing users to program and manipulate digital ink directly through touch and pen interactions rather than traditional text-based coding.

Designed to support the early stages of the creative process, Playbook prioritizes a "blank page" experience by replacing traditional UI menus with transient, gesture-based controls. The interface aims to avoid the high latency and ambiguity of AI-driven tools, focusing instead on immediate, tactile feedback that mimics the spontaneity of physical paper.

entry.title: Veloren Technical Implementation: ECS, Voxel Storage, and Procedural Generation
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | blog.jsbarretto.com | discussion | hacker news

The architecture utilizes an Entity Component System (ECS) to facilitate high-concurrency multiplayer environments and a custom "chonks" data structure to optimize voxel storage and random access. World generation is driven by physically-based hydraulic erosion and low-resolution pre-generation, allowing for features such as continuous river systems and extended view distances.

A real-time simulation system (RTSim) enables the engine to track NPC movement, faction dynamics, and economic shifts even when players are not in the vicinity. The engine also employs a unified controller system that ensures players and NPCs interact with the physics engine using identical movement logic.

Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

The Symbiosis update, arriving December 8, will introduce a permanent PvE experience, marking a departure from the game's original strict extraction shooter vision. This transition also includes an end to the studio's strict seasonal release schedule to allow for more flexible development and testing.

This pivot follows significant workforce reductions at Bungie and the decision to end live development for *Destiny 2*. The studio aims to address player requests for greater depth and variety through this new development model and an evolving gameplay loop.

entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer has stated that the studio's hiring process includes reviewing social media accounts, noting that candidates who are vocal against crunch culture are often not hired. Brammer described the studio's environment as one centered on high-intensity work and expected overtime.

To compensate for intensive work periods, the studio provides financial incentives such as bonuses and shares, which Brammer claims can result in life-changing wealth for long-term employees. These comments come as the studio continues to navigate a culture of high-intensity work and periodic layoffs, having reduced its workforce by approximately 20 percent annually over the last six years.

entry.title: Superpose Launches AI-Powered Posing Guide for iOS
entry.content:
TechCrunch AI | techcrunch.com | source

Developed by former TikTok employees Melody Chu and Jing Liu, the iOS app Superpose uses generative AI to provide real-time posing guidance for photography. The application analyzes a user's photo or selfie to generate four AI-driven pose suggestions, allowing users to align themselves with those suggestions via a "match-pose" feature.

The startup has secured $2.2 million in funding from Khosla Ventures, Meitu, and OVTR VC. While many AI-driven photography tools focus on generating artificial backgrounds or fantastical environments, Superpose aims to improve natural portraiture by coaching users during the actual moment of capture.

entry.title: Steam Frame VR Headset Pricing and Reservation Details Revealed
entry.content:
Techmeme | theshortcut.com | source | hacker news

Valve has announced the pricing and reservation process for the Steam Frame, a standalone VR headset. The device will be available in two configurations: a 256GB model starting at $1,059 and a 1TB model for $1,299. Both versions include a copy of Half-Life: Alyx. Interested users can sign up for a reservation on Steam until September 17, after which a randomized lottery will determine the first wave of buyers. Purchase invites are expected to begin on September 21.

The headset features a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 processor, 16GB of LPDDR5X RAM, and pancake lenses with up to 110-degree field of view. The display offers a resolution of 2160x2160 per eye with refresh rates ranging from 72Hz to 144Hz. The device includes eye tracking and a wireless adapter for low-latency PC connection.

entry.title: Laurelyn McWills Discusses Integrating Emotional Connections into Game Systems
entry.content:
GDC Videos | youtube.com

Designing game systems to elicit specific player emotions allows developers to address fundamental human needs through core gameplay mechanics. Laurelyn McWills advocates for "experiential core loops" that connect psychological motivations—such as agency, mastery, or social connection—directly to systemic rewards and player interactions.

Using case studies from Full Spectrum Warrior and Free Realms, McWills demonstrates how systemic changes, such as mission-based rescue objectives and social-based leveling, can maintain immersion and reinforce emotional engagement. Her approach moves beyond traditional combat loops to create a tighter connection between player motivation and gameplay mechanics.

Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

The worker-run indie studio behind *Goodbye Volcano High* and *Young Suns* has laid off 13 employees, including team leads and elected executives. entry.title: xkcd Fonts Derived from Randall Munroe's Handwriting
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | github.com | discussion

Two typefaces based on the handwriting of xkcd creator Randall Munroe are available in this repository. The collection includes `xkcd Script`, a less uniform typeface designed to resemble a natural script, and a more legible, uniform version titled `xkcd`.

The `xkcd` font was originally used in the 2013 webcomic "The Pace of Modern Life." Both fonts are provided in TTF, WOFF, and OTF formats under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 3.0 License.
